clue.text: Returned volume I am studying that graphically conveys feeling

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'something that graphically conveys feeling'

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the book word is read from its end

blocks.note: a tome is a large book, a volume
taken as written
to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: Someone back with a library book is reading about how images can express emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: An emoticon is a small typed face or picture used in messages to show the writer's mood.

clue.text: Duck seized by male or female raptor or other bird

indicators.note: what is seized is held inside its captors, so the duck goes within the next letters

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like O
taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female
an owl is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A duck is snatched by a bird of prey, cock or hen, or by some other bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The duck goes in right after the male letter. 'Other' marks this bird as different from the duck and raptor already named.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorfowl is another name for the red grouse, a game bird of upland heather moors.

clue.text: Caught up with small fraud that's handled in court

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are written from bottom to top

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
something caught like a fish is in a net
a racket is a swindle or dishonest scheme

explanation.surface: A petty swindler has been caught out and is now facing trial in a law court.
explanation.walkthrough: The S and IN NET together are reversed before RACKET is added. The court is not a law court but a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis racket is held in the hand by a player on a tennis court, the sporting sense of court.

clue.text: Put men on board lacking refinement, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word's sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: crude means coarse or unrefined

explanation.surface: Someone staffed a ship with rough and uncultured sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: To crew a vessel is to supply it with sailors, so a crewed ship had its men put aboard.

clue.text: Celebrity from Argentina met again in Latin America

indicators.note: taken from the run of letters, so the answer sits within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A star from Argentina was met once more somewhere in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The same answer is hidden a second time, in 'Latin America', which is what 'again in' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: A big name is a famous person, so name alone serves as a synonym for a celebrity.

clue.text: Burns, for example, most dreadfully apparent in examination

indicators.note: done dreadfully means done badly, leaving the letters jumbled
seen inside something, so the scrambled letters sit within the test word

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
a scan is a close inspection or medical examination

explanation.surface: Burn injuries look at their worst when a doctor examines them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burns' reads as injuries, but it is Robert Burns, the Scottish national poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns was a native of Scotland, so he is an example of a man from that country.

clue.text: Appear satisfied as setter, say — finish off clue and carry on

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a contented dog such as a setter wags its tail
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A crossword setter, pleased with a clue, wraps it up and keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is the dog breed, not the crossword compiler the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To wage a war or campaign is to conduct it, to carry it on.

clue.text: Military guard posted on line given new order

indicators.note: putting something in a new order rearranges it

blocks.note: a letter posted is sent
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier on guard duty was stationed on the front line under fresh orders.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a soldier stationed to keep watch, a sentry.

clue.text: Correct a Conservative junior minister?

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a curate is an assistant to a parish priest, a junior minister of religion

explanation.surface: Is this the right description of a young Tory government minister?
explanation.walkthrough: The minister is a church minister, not a government one.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate and correct are synonyms meaning free from error.

clue.text: Way of doing things aboard satellite

blocks.note: MO is modus operandi, a method of working
aboard means on a ship or vehicle

explanation.surface: How things are done on board a space satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moon is Earth's natural satellite, and any moon orbits a planet.

clue.text: Odd statement on novel in book collection

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the word comes out in an unusual arrangement

blocks.note: novel means new
all nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange remark about a novel appears in an anthology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in an across clue puts the anagram after the other piece. 'Novel' looks like a book in a collection, but it only means new.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament is the collection of twenty-seven books forming the second part of the Christian Bible.

clue.text: Communist comrades constituting funny foursome

blocks.note: Karl Marx, the founder of communism
comrades in a union or cause are brothers

explanation.surface: Fellow communists make up a group of four comedians.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marx Brothers were a family comedy act of four brothers in their best-known films: Groucho, Chico, Harpo and Zeppo.

clue.text: Judge making criminal face right

blocks.note: a con is a convict
a face of a cube or building is a side
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A judge forces a criminal to face up to doing right.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider something is to judge or regard it a certain way, as in considering a plan wise.

clue.text: Frenchman who composed party line

blocks.note: a rave is a large dance party
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A French composer wrote a song with a party theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Ravel was a French composer, best known for his orchestral piece Boléro.

clue.text: Border force repelled with spirit

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: to ram is to force or drive hard
gin is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: A border guard unit fought off invaders with great spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border force' reads as the UK customs agency, but the two words belong to different parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is the edge or border of a page or area.

clue.text: High jumper that's exemplarily fit

blocks.note: first meaning: an insect famous for leaping many times its own height
second meaning: the creature in the idiom for being in top condition

explanation.walkthrough: The high jumper sounds like an athlete, which is why being fit seems to follow. The idiom 'fit as a flea' means very healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny parasitic insect that leaps prodigiously, and the standard of fitness in a well-known saying.

clue.text: Walk-on parts for boxer? Few as pro, oddly

indicators.note: arranged oddly means put in a strange order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: all eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A boxer rarely gets bit parts in films once turned professional.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer is the dog breed, and its walk-on parts are the feet it walks on, not small acting roles.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's front feet are its forepaws, the parts it walks on.

clue.text: Number that's small, like six or eight

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
six and eight are both even numbers

explanation.surface: A low number that sits somewhere between six and eight.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites the number between six and eight, which happens to be the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven is a cardinal number, the one after six.

clue.text: It's smart including our squadrons for aerial attack

indicators.note: a word that includes something holds it within its own letters

blocks.note: smart and sting both mean to hurt sharply
the Royal Air Force, Britain's own air arm

explanation.surface: It is clever to deploy our air force squadrons for an air raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' reads as clever, but it is the verb meaning to hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Strafing is attacking ground targets with machine-gun fire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Loud cry as announcement of delivery

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out, so it is the sound of the word that counts

blocks.note: in cricket a bowler's delivery is a ball

explanation.surface: A newborn's first loud cry announces the birth.
explanation.walkthrough: Delivery suggests childbirth, but it is a ball bowled at cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A bawl is a loud howling cry, as of a child.

clue.text: Songbird needing warmth wrapped in clothing

indicators.note: something wrapped in a covering sits inside it

blocks.note: wear is clothing, as in menswear
heat is warmth

explanation.surface: A small bird in cold weather needs to be bundled up for warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small migratory songbird of the thrush family with a white rump.

clue.text: Private resentment expressed

indicators.note: something expressed is put into speech, so its sound is meant

blocks.note: first meaning: a soldier serving in the ranks rather than as an officer
rancour is bitter resentment

explanation.surface: Hidden bitterness is finally voiced.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent rancour and the answer sound alike. 'Private' looks like an adjective about the resentment, but it is the army rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranker is an enlisted soldier, one of the rank and file, such as a private.

clue.text: Remaining English newspaper grabbed by fan

indicators.note: what is grabbed is held inside the grabber

blocks.note: a fan is a lover of something
E is the abbreviation for English
the FT is the Financial Times, a London newspaper

explanation.surface: An admirer snatched the last copy of an English paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftover describes something remaining unused, such as food after a meal.

clue.text: Woollen coat to take to the cleaners

blocks.note: first meaning: the wool covering a sheep
second meaning: to swindle someone out of money

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction to dry-clean a wool coat; the cleaners idiom means to cheat someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a sheep's woolly coat; the verb means to overcharge or swindle, which is what taking someone to the cleaners means.

clue.text: Not complete address for article, for instance

blocks.note: only part of something, not the whole
an address is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A speech was given in shortened form for a newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: The article is the grammatical one, a word like 'the' or 'a', not a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Articles are one of the grammatical classes of words, alongside nouns and verbs.

clue.text: Piece of music from Agra, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several possible arrangements of the letters

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A tune that may have come from the Indian city of Agra.
explanation.definitionFit: A raga is a melodic framework for improvisation in Indian classical music, and a piece built on it.

clue.text: Wine, such as Bordeaux or Malaga

blocks.note: first meaning: a sweet fortified wine from Portugal
second meaning: harbour towns, each an example of the category

explanation.walkthrough: Bordeaux and Malaga are both famous wine names, but here they are harbour cities in France and Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Port is a fortified wine, and it is also a harbour town such as Bordeaux or Malaga.

clue.text: Scrutinises start of election very well

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
'very well' is a phrase of agreement, like yes

explanation.surface: Someone checks the opening of an election result very carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it closely, so eyes means scrutinises.

clue.text: Driver of vehicle in which composer covers journey

indicators.note: a cover goes around what it covers, so one word encloses another

blocks.note: Richard Wagner, the German opera composer
a go is a turn or trip, and to go is to journey

explanation.surface: A musician travels long distances in a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A waggoner drives a wagon, a horse-drawn goods vehicle.

clue.text: Doctor almost presented with certain prize

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: to doctor is to treat medically
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A medic was nearly handed a guaranteed award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person but works as a verb here. 'Prize' is the verb, to value highly.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure something is to prize it, to value it greatly.
